title: Forty-one years, 30 moments
lede: From a Commodore bulletin board to an Italian software holding company. Pick a thread to filter.

events.title: Incorporated as Quantum Computer Services
events.text: A Delaware company whose first service, Q-Link, is for owners of Commodore computers.

events.title: “America Online” and “You’ve Got Mail”
events.text: Quantum introduces a nationwide service under the America Online name in October. Elwood Edwards records the greetings on a cassette deck at home.

events.title: The company takes the name of its service
events.text: Quantum Computer Services becomes America Online, Inc.

events.title: Initial public offering
events.text: AOL sells stock to the public for the first time. It ends the fiscal year with 182,000 subscribers.

events.title: The first mass mailing of trial disks
events.text: About 200,000 floppy disks go out. The response rate, by the account of the executive who ran it, is 10%.

events.title: 3.0 million subscribers
events.text: More than three times the 903,000 of a year earlier.

events.title: 6.2 million subscribers and $1.09 billion in revenue
events.text: Marketing costs for the year are $212.7 million.

events.title: $385.2 million of marketing costs written off
events.text: AOL stops capitalizing subscriber acquisition costs and expenses the whole balance.

events.title: Flat-rate pricing: $19.95 a month, unlimited
events.text: Usage jumps and members begin to get busy signals.

events.title: Agreement with 36 state attorneys general
events.text: AOL agrees to refunds, easier cancellation and a pause in advertising for February.

events.title: CompuServe
events.text: AOL acquires CompuServe’s online service, which has about 2.1 million subscribers that June.

events.title: Price rises to $21.95
events.text: The increase takes effect at each member’s April billing date.

events.title: ICQ
events.text: AOL pays $287 million in cash, with up to $120 million more contingent, for Mirabilis, maker of ICQ.

events.title: Netscape
events.text: AOL completes its merger with Netscape, issuing about 95 million shares.

events.title: AOL agrees to merge with Time Warner
events.text: An all-stock deal worth more than $160 billion at that day’s prices. AOL shareholders are to own about 55%.

events.title: AOL Time Warner begins
events.text: The merger closes. The cost of acquiring Time Warner is recorded at about $147 billion.

events.title: The peak: 26.7 million U.S. subscribers
events.text: The year-end count is 26.5 million.

events.title: A $98.7 billion net loss
events.text: Goodwill and intangible write-downs total $99.8 billion. The SEC and the Department of Justice are investigating AOL’s accounting.

events.title: “AOL” is dropped from the parent’s name
events.text: AOL Time Warner Inc. becomes Time Warner Inc.

events.title: Google agrees to buy 5% of AOL for $1 billion
events.text: The stake is issued in April 2006. Time Warner buys it back in July 2009 for $283 million.

events.title: AOL goes free for broadband users
events.text: Software and e-mail are given away to anyone with a connection. U.S. subscribers end the year at 13.2 million, from 19.5 million.

events.title: Bebo
events.text: AOL pays $852 million in cash for the social network. Time Warner records a $2.2 billion impairment of AOL goodwill for the year.

events.title: Spun off from Time Warner
events.text: Shareholders receive one AOL share for every eleven Time Warner shares. AOL has 5.0 million subscribers and about 6,700 employees.

events.title: The Huffington Post
events.text: Acquired for $295.5 million, net of cash acquired.

events.title: 2.2 million subscribers
events.text: Subscription revenue is $606.5 million of a $2.53 billion total.

events.title: Verizon agrees to buy AOL
events.text: $50 a share, about $4.4 billion.

events.title: Oath
events.text: Verizon closes its purchase of Yahoo and combines it with AOL.

events.title: AOL Instant Messenger shuts down
events.text: Announced on October 6, 2017.

events.title: Apollo completes its purchase
events.text: $5 billion for Verizon’s media business, which takes the name Yahoo. Verizon keeps 10%.

events.title: Dial-up is discontinued
events.text: The AOL Dialer software and the AOL Shield browser go with it.

events.title: Bending Spoons completes its purchase
events.text: $1,456 million in cash for AOL Holdco I LLC. The deal was announced on October 29, 2025.
